FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 October 1979, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Insulation Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnica Division Council. 0.2 This standard deals with built-up mica or treated mica paper for use in electrical equipment. It consists of the following three parts: Part I Part II Definitions and General Requirements, Materials. for rigid mica Methods of Test, and Part III Specifications for Individual

0.1 This

0.3 This standard ( Part III/%- 1 ) covers requirements materials for commutators separators.

0.4 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from Publication 371-3-1 ( i973 ) Specification for insulating materials based on built-up mica or treated mica paper: Part 3 Specifications for individual materials: Sheet 1 : Rigid mica materiak for commutator separators, issued by the International Electrotechnicai Commission ( IEC ). 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shail be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960". The. number of significant .places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1.1 This standard (Part III/&c 1 ) applies to rigid mica sheets for commutator separators supplied either 2s sheets or as separators cut to size. 1.2 The thickness of the sheets is from O-3 mm to 2 mm and they are made of muscovite or phlogopite mica built-up from bonded splittings. 2. GENERAL REQYIRE-TS hardness, free from

2.1 The material 2s supplied shall be of uniform soft patches and foreign matter.

2.2 The bonding medium used shall be agreed between supplier and purchaser. The material when tested in accordance with the methods given, shall comply with all the-requirements of this specification. 3. MARKING 3.1 1Vhen commutator separators are delivered in stacks, each stack shall he marked with the nominal thickness of the separators and the number of separators in the stack. 3.2 When commutator separators are required `to be delivered in gauged stacks ( see4.2 ), each stack shall be marked with the nominal thickness of the separators, the number in the stack and the stack height. 3.3 For other forms of delivery, the nominal thickness ( S.S 4.1) and the number of separators or sheets shall be stated. 4. THLCKNESS 4.1 Rigid mica material shall be supplied either as sheets or strips or small separators cut to.size with an area less than or equal to 10 ems. 4.1.1 Ajparatus -The thickness of the material as received shall be measured with an apparatus in accordance with 2.1 of Part II of this standard. The pressure exerted on the specimens 600 N/cm2 or as mutually agreed to between supplier. 4.1.2 Test Specimens - The test with 2.2 of Part II of this standard. specimens 4 shall be 10 N/cm2 to the purchaser and the be in accordance

4.2.1.1 The thickness measurement on commutator separators shall be made under a pressure of 3 000 N/cm2 on stacks of at least 20 separators, or as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

4.2.X.2 When commutator separators over 10 cm% in area are not required to *be stack gauged, they shall comply with the requirements of 4.1.3.1 and 4.1.4. 4.2.1.3 The separators may, if desired, be interleaved densified paper with a thickness of about 0.02 mm. 5 by a piece of

Is : 9299 ( Part III/Set 1) - 1979 45.1.4 All the separators in the stack to be tested shall be aligned, and the stack subjected to a pressure of 3 000 N/cm2 in a direction perpendicular to the surface of the separators and uniformly distributed over the surface of the separators. 4.2.1.5 The measurement is made at a temperature in the range of 15�C to 35�C with an accuracy of 605 mm on a press with plane parallel plates. 4.2.1.6 The thickness d of a stack is given by: d = dl - d2 where dl = thickness of a stack interleaves, and of II separators and (n1)

dz = total thickness of (a - 1 ) interleaves obtained by measuring a stack of ( rl - 1 ) interleaves with a surface of 0'01 m2 placed on a steel block with a surface of @Ol m2 and a height of 60 mm under a pressure of 3 000 N/cmz.
Note - If no interleaves are used, the second measurement is done with steel block only for reasons of checking the deformation of the press. the
